items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had met "Bull" a few years before when Edgar Courance and I had made friends with a couple of amateur musicians from Hamilton, Ohio, and we would go there for a couple of days every week and play in a small cabaret.

ctx.x: A person was allowed two 2 quarts of whiskey or other alchohol drinks a month and could only buy it at government stores. One could also have a case of 12 bottles of beer and there was one label called White Horse Ale that I could get a fine feeling from after I drank two bottles. There were 4 of us staying at the same place, so we had no worries about drinks as we had 8 quarts of whiskey and 48 bottles of beer between us for the month and none of us were really heavy drinkers although I had learned to drink and…

John Williams got homesick for New York and eventually left the band and another sax-player from Louisville named Lester Carr took his place. The next one to leave the band was Hubert Mann. He received an offer to join Speed Webb's orchestra in California, so Rudolph "Bull" Williams, [who] lived in a town not far from Springfield was hired as banjoist.

Rudolph was a very stocky young fellow who had played football at Wilberforce College and because of his big face, big hands and broad shoulders, he was given the name of "Bull". His father was a preacher but "Bull" was everything except religious. I had met "Bull" a few years before when Edgar Courance and I had made friends with a couple of amateur musicians from Hamilton, Ohio, and we would go there for a couple of days every week and play in a small cabaret.
